title: Using Core-ERP - process overview
intro: This guide describes the practical sequence from technical preparation to daily accounting. It is based on application source reviewed on 14 October 2026; the sequence is recommended operating guidance, not evidence that a live organisation has been configured or tested.
steps: Technical preparation: establish tenant access, initialise the application schema, and initialise the template organisation if a reusable starting configuration is required.
Organisation setup: create the operating organisation; copy selected template setup or configure it manually; review divisions, currencies, tax and fiscal calendars.
Control configuration: establish permission roles, modules, resource roles and workflows before giving users operational access.
Model configuration: review object types and schemas, numbering, the chart of accounts, transaction types and posting lines.
Master data: create legal entities, people, dimension records, bank and other sub-ledger accounts, and the accounting objects needed for transactions.
Execution: capture balanced transactions, complete the configured workflow, post, reconcile and report.
check: Keep the operating organisation distinct from TEMPLATE. Use the later reference sections to inspect seeded definitions; seeded names alone do not establish complete business-process automation.

title: 1. Technical initialisation
intro: Perform these steps with the access required by the setup actions. They prepare the ERP application and reusable template, rather than recording normal business activity.
steps: Sign in through Core, select the intended tenant and launch Core-ERP. Establish who is responsible for ERP setup administration and confirm that the existing ERP database connection is available.

Use Initialise Schema. The application executes schema/erp-schema.sql through its existing API and Broker connection. In development/test, use this action for agreed schema changes; do not use a separate SQL-client update or migration step.

Use Initialise Template Org when template defaults are needed. This creates or rebuilds the tenant's TEMPLATE organisation, its root division and seeded configuration. The action requires confirmation and ERP Setup Administrator access.

Treat repeated template initialisation as a reset/rebuild operation. The current implementation resets existing template data before rebuilding definitions; do not use it as routine synchronisation of a customised template.

Optionally run template example initialisation after TEMPLATE exists. This is a separate administrator action requiring confirmation. It creates example records and then applies example-record bindings to transaction line classifications.
Review the resulting template before copying from it. Identify which modules, accounts, types, workflows, fiscal settings and reports are suitable for the new operating organisation.
check: Schema initialisation has completed successfully; TEMPLATE exists if required; example data was either deliberately added or deliberately omitted. No schema or initialisation action was executed in producing this document.

title: 2. Create and configure the operating organisation
intro: Organisation setup establishes the scope and reference data for business records and transactions.
steps: Create a new organisation with a unique code, name and chosen base currency. Leave it as an operating organisation rather than a template. Creation provides a ROOT division and assigns the creator the initial Security Administrator role.

Choose between copying selected setup from TEMPLATE and building it manually. In Copy Organisation Setup, confirm source and target and review every selected category. Copying can update matching configuration and can include business records and user-role assignments; do not treat it as definitions-only by default.
Review organisation identification and optional icon settings. Establish the division hierarchy and legal responsibility for each operating area. Keep divisions within the organisation and tenant.
Configure the countries and currencies needed for operations. Review currency precision and display formatting, then establish the required currency-pair exchange-rate entries and effective dates.

Configure tax types and rates for the organisation's actual transactions. Review effective dates and line-level tax expectations; seeded rates are starting configuration, not an approval of tax treatment.

Create or review fiscal years and their periods. Replace copied example calendars with the dates and statuses appropriate to the organisation. Establish which periods are available for capture and posting.
Select required modules and review financial statement formats and report definitions. Confirm their references to the organisation's chart and object model.
check: The intended organisation and division can be selected; base currency, tax settings and fiscal calendar are agreed; copied setup has been reviewed before operational use.

title: 3. Roles, access and resources
intro: Permission roles control user access. Resource roles describe business responsibilities assigned to people. Maintain the distinction even where one person performs both roles.
steps: Review or create permission roles for setup administration, security administration, record maintenance, transaction capture, review, posting and reporting as required by the organisation.

Map roles to modules and configure resource permissions for the relevant organisation, division, object or transaction type, workflow status and permitted action. Module membership alone does not grant every operation.
Assign users to permission roles with the intended validity dates. Review copied user assignments explicitly rather than accepting the template's users as the operating organisation's access policy.
Set division scope and whether permissions apply to child divisions. Confirm that ordinary users can reach the required modules and that restricted records and actions remain unavailable.

Configure separate resource roles, their module/type relationships and assignment expectations. Create the people/resource records needed for ownership, responsibility, approvals and operational assignments.
Assign resources to the appropriate objects with applicable validity dates. Resource assignments do not replace permission-role assignments or workflow-action access.
check: Each operating responsibility has a named owner; user role assignments, division scope, module access and workflow action roles have been reviewed. Perform practical access checks before rollout.

title: 4. Workflows and record readiness
intro: Workflows define how records and transactions move through controlled states. The available steps and action labels depend on the selected configuration.
steps: Review workflow statuses, paths, steps and allowed transitions. Define the intended creation, review, approval, rejection and completion routes for the relevant object and transaction classes.
Assign permission roles to workflow actions and ensure the users performing those actions also have the applicable module and resource permissions.
Connect each supported object type and transaction type to its appropriate workflow path. Confirm the path is active and contains a usable initial state and the intended transitions.

For master records, review which configured statuses enable use in transactions. Complete the required workflow before expecting a bank account, asset, accounting object or dimension to be selectable and usable.

For financial transactions, review the route to submission and posting. The current journal implementation revalidates the journal, period availability and allocation-record usability on transitions to submitted or posted.
Retain action comments and review workflow history when investigating changes. Do not assume that every seeded type uses identical action names or the same approval sequence.
check: Required paths are attached, actions have assigned roles, and at least one authorised user can perform each necessary transition. Operational master records reach statuses enabled for use.

title: 5. Object types and reusable schemas
intro: Configure definitions before creating the business records they govern. Prefer the shared ERP model to separate feature-specific account models.
steps: Review sub-ledger types for balance-sheet allocations: for example bank, customer, vendor, cash point, asset and loan accounts. Set whether legal-entity linkage and other class-specific requirements apply.

Review accounting-object types for income-statement allocations: for example property, operational project, contract and maintenance order. Review parent relationships and required links to other records.

Review accounting-dimension types for classification across either category: for example service, revenue type, measurement unit and insurance cover type. Dimensions do not replace allocation to sub-ledgers or accounting objects.

Review each custom schema's tabs, scalar fields, grids, required markers, allowed values, validation, reference targets and presentation settings. Use the complete schema reference later in this document.
Review manual or automatic numbering, ranges and uniqueness expectations. Use the existing numbering mechanism; do not allocate codes independently in spreadsheets or browser code.
Map types to the relevant modules, resource roles and workflow paths. Establish the prerequisite reference records for each schema before creating dependent records.

Confirm which seeded types are actually needed. A type definition is a reusable record structure; it does not mean depreciation, valuation, lease calculation or every domain workflow is automatically executed.
check: Required types and schemas are agreed; reference targets and numbering are valid; workflow and module relationships are ready for record creation.

title: 6. Chart of accounts and transaction configuration
intro: GL accounts determine posting and reporting. Object types and dimensions provide separate allocation and classification information.
steps: Review GL account types and their financial-reporting categories. Create, import or review all GL accounts required by the organisation's selected processes and reports, rather than every possible seeded account.
Set GL-level sub-ledger requirements and any required sub-ledger type. Ensure financial statement formats and reports classify the chart correctly.
Review transaction groups and create or adapt the transaction types needed for operations. Set module relationships, workflow paths and whether additional capture lines are permitted.
For each transaction type, review every line's order, code, description, GL account, debit/credit side and required, optional or repeatable occurrence.

Review amount sources: distinguish manually entered amounts from configured generated balancing amounts. Do not assume that schema values or supporting grid totals automatically generate journal postings.
Configure required or permitted sub-ledger types, accounting-object types and dimension types. Review captured, defaulted or fixed value behaviour and any specific record bindings.
Resolve defaults pointing to template or example records before using the operating organisation. Verify linked-object consistency where two allocations describe related records.
Use representative balanced journals to review the intended accounting result, access, fiscal restrictions and reporting treatment before routine capture.
check: Every required line references an existing GL account; allocation rules and any record bindings are valid; the workflow can reach posting; representative accounting results are agreed.

title: 7. Create operational master records
intro: Create the full set of records needed for the organisation's selected business processes. Follow the actual schema references; the order below is a practical dependency sequence rather than a universal rule for every type.
steps: Complete prerequisite reference configuration: divisions, countries, currencies, taxes, fiscal periods, modules, roles, workflow paths, types and GL accounts.

Create all required legal entities, including the operating entity, banks, customers, suppliers and other counterparties where applicable. Capture identifications, addresses and relationships before linking dependent accounts.
Create people/resources and the required accounting-dimension records. Populate their custom details, including units, service characteristics, mapping grids and reference rates where relevant.
Create required bank and cash-point sub-ledger accounts. Complete bank details, currency, contacts and legal-entity links where the type requires them.
Create customer, vendor, employee and loan sub-ledger accounts as needed. Link existing legal entities and resources where applicable and capture the type-specific data.

Create asset and capital-project sub-ledger accounts for the relevant balance-sheet allocations. Record acquisition/lifecycle details and supporting grids; these details do not themselves calculate or post journal amounts.

Create accounting objects such as properties, cost centres, profit centres, operational projects, contracts, policies and operational records. Create referenced records first, then dependent records; for example establish a policy before a claim that requires it.
Complete configured workflow actions so records are enabled for use. Review effective dates, resource assignments, documents and related-object links before transaction capture.

Where opening balances are required, define and review the balanced opening journal and its permitted fiscal period, GL accounts and allocations. Creating a master record does not establish an accounting balance.
check: The required chart, legal entities, resources, dimension records, bank accounts, assets and accounting objects exist in the operating organisation and are usable under their workflows.

title: 8. Capture, progress and post transactions
intro: Transaction capture turns the configured posting structure and operational master records into balanced accounting entries.
steps: Select the correct tenant, organisation and source division. Choose the transaction type, journal date, fiscal period, currency, exchange rate and meaningful description.
Review the transaction type's configured lines. Include required lines, use optional and repeatable lines as applicable, and add extra lines only where permitted.
Enter manual amounts on the configured debit or credit side. Review generated balancing amounts where configured and confirm that the final journal balances.

Select required sub-ledger accounts for balance-sheet allocations and accounting objects for income-statement allocations. Select required dimensions for classification. Observe both GL-account and line-definition requirements.

Check that all linked records belong to the applicable scope, are enabled for use and are consistent with related allocations. Include supporting documents or notes through the available application facilities where required.
Save the journal. The current save path requires balanced debits and credits; do not rely on saving an incomplete, unbalanced draft for later completion.
Use the configured workflow actions for submission, review and posting. The exact action labels and intermediate states come from the transaction type's path and the user's permissions.

Before submission/posting, confirm the fiscal period permits the action. The current implementation permits open and soft_closed periods and rejects closed or locked periods; define an operating policy consistent with that behaviour.

After posting, record the journal reference and review its detail and history. Posted journals cannot be edited or moved to another workflow status through the current journal endpoints; use an authorised corrective transaction where appropriate.
check: The intended journal is posted, balanced and correctly allocated; currency and period settings are correct; workflow history identifies the actions performed.

title: 9. Reporting, reconciliation and ongoing operation
intro: Use reporting and controlled maintenance to confirm that operational activity produces the intended financial result.
steps: Run the trial balance, relevant financial statements and configured operational reports for the intended organisation, division scope and fiscal range. Confirm the report's status and filtering rules rather than assuming every report includes the same journals.

Reconcile bank, cash, receivable, payable, asset and loan balances to supporting records. Investigate unexpected GL balances, missing allocations and discrepancies between operational data and posted transactions.
Review period status as part of the agreed closing process. Set the next period's availability deliberately and account for the current soft_closed behaviour when designing cut-off controls.

Maintain currencies and exchange rates using effective dates. For a correction, use the existing revision/history process and reason; create a new entry if the currency pair or effective date changes.
Maintain record versions, effective dates, resource assignments and reference links. A current record view does not replace the historical context of a saved version.
Review roles, module access and workflow action assignments as responsibilities change. Keep resource roles separate from access control.

Review proposed changes to types, schemas, transaction lines and reports together. In development/test apply agreed database changes using Initialise Schema; template reinitialisation remains a deliberate reset/rebuild, not daily maintenance.
check: Reports and reconciliations agree with expected accounting results; exceptions have owners; the next operating period and configuration changes are controlled.
